digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center transport / rate-limit handling
propositions: Jira Data Center built-in rate-limiting (per-user token bucket, enabled by admin) causes hard failures when 429 responses are received, propagating as JIRAError instead of being honoured via Retry-After header

429 retry must be scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS only because the single transport choke point _with_connection_retry fronts all 15 call sites including mutations, and retrying after a 429 that arrived post-write would reintroduce duplicate-issue class bugs
Retry-After header handling must reuse existing parse_retry_after and MAX_BACKOFF_S, apply jitter-then-clamp (min(60s, retry_after * (1 + random 0-20%))), and default to opt-in OFF for all call sites

The implementation required splitting into two independent changes: S1 extract retry/error cluster to new module (forced by 800-line cap on transport.py with 11-line headroom), and S2 add 429 policy in extracted module with per-call opt-in mechanism
Exhausted-cap path must raise BackendHTTPError(code=429) via existing _as_backend_http_error translation, never raw JIRAError, to preserve the adapter boundary contract
